title: Panaji, Goa's capital
text: Panaji, also called Panjim, is the capital city of Goa.
aliases: What is the capital of Goa?

title: Goa's districts
text: Goa's government describes North Goa and South Goa and identifies Kushavati as the newest district.

title: Vasco da Gama
text: Vasco da Gama is an industrial town on the Mormugao peninsula and is associated with Mormugao harbour.

title: Margao
text: Margao is the principal commercial town of South Goa and is also known as Madgaon.

title: Mapusa
text: Mapusa is a North Goa market town known for its Friday market.

title: Old Goa
text: Old Goa was the capital under Portuguese rule until the capital shifted to Panjim in 1843.

title: Goa Liberation
text: Goa became part of the Indian Union on 19 December 1961 following Operation Vijay.

title: Goa statehood
text: Goa became India's twenty-fifth state on 30 May 1987.

title: Portuguese heritage
text: Portuguese rule began with the capture of Goa in 1510 and left a visible legacy in the state's churches, houses and urban form.

title: Basilica of Bom Jesus
text: The Basilica of Bom Jesus is one of the churches in the UNESCO-listed Churches and Convents of Goa at Old Goa.
source_name: UNESCO — Churches and Convents of Goa

title: Se Cathedral
text: Se Cathedral is part of the UNESCO-listed group of churches and convents at Old Goa.
source_name: UNESCO — Churches and Convents of Goa

title: Fontainhas
text: Fontainhas is Panaji's historic Latin Quarter, noted for colourful houses and Portuguese-influenced streetscapes.

title: Fort Aguada
text: Fort Aguada is a seventeenth-century Portuguese fort overlooking the Arabian Sea and the Mandovi estuary.
source_name: NRI Commission, Government of Goa — Forts

title: Chapora Fort
text: Chapora Fort stands above the Chapora River and offers views toward Vagator and the Arabian Sea.

title: Dudhsagar Falls
text: Dudhsagar Falls is a four-tiered waterfall on the Mandovi River in the Bhagwan Mahavir wildlife area.

title: Mandovi River
text: The Mandovi is one of Goa's major rivers and reaches the Arabian Sea near Panaji.

title: Zuari River
text: The Zuari is one of Goa's major rivers and forms an important estuarine system in the state.

title: Calangute Beach
text: Calangute is a prominent North Goa beach on the Arabian Sea coast.

title: Baga Beach
text: Baga is a North Goa beach adjoining the Calangute stretch.
source_name: NRI Commission, Government of Goa — Beaches

title: Anjuna Beach
text: Anjuna is a North Goa coastal village and beach associated with a long-running flea market.
source_name: NRI Commission, Government of Goa — Beaches

title: Vagator Beach
text: Vagator is a North Goa beach below the headland crowned by Chapora Fort.
source_name: NRI Commission, Government of Goa — Beaches

title: Palolem Beach
text: Palolem is a crescent-shaped beach in Canacona in South Goa.
source_name: NRI Commission, Government of Goa — Beaches

title: Colva Beach
text: Colva is a broad sandy beach in South Goa, close to Margao.

title: Goa Carnival
text: Goa Carnival is a pre-Lenten celebration marked by public parades, music and performance.
source_name: Goa Department of Information — People of Goa

title: São João
text: São João is celebrated in Goa during the monsoon and is associated with community festivities and traditional well-jumping.

title: Shigmo
text: Shigmo is a major Goan spring festival featuring processions, folk dance and music.
source_name: Goa Department of Information — People of Goa

title: Ganesh Chaturthi in Goa
text: Ganesh Chaturthi, locally called Chavoth, is widely celebrated by Goan families.
source_name: Goa Department of Information — People of Goa

title: Goan cuisine
text: Goan cuisine reflects coastal ingredients and varied Hindu and Christian culinary traditions.
source_name: Goa Department of Information — People of Goa

title: Fish curry rice
text: Rice with fish curry, commonly called xit kodi, is described as a staple Goan meal.
source_name: Goa Department of Information — People of Goa

title: Xacuti
text: Xacuti is a Goan curry style known for a complex roasted-spice and coconut base.
source_name: Government of Goa — Culture and Tourism

title: Vindaloo
text: Vindaloo is a Goan meat preparation whose name and style reflect Portuguese and local culinary influences.
source_name: Government of Goa — Culture and Tourism

title: Bebinca
text: Bebinca is a layered Goan dessert traditionally made with ingredients including coconut milk, eggs, sugar and flour.
source_name: Government of Goa — Culture and Tourism

title: Feni
text: Feni is a spirit associated with Goa and is made from cashew apples or coconut palm sap.

title: Tiatr
text: Tiatr is a popular form of Konkani musical theatre supported by the Tiatr Academy of Goa.

title: Konkani
text: Konkani is Goa's official language; Marathi is also used for official purposes under state law.

title: Goan music
text: Goa's musical traditions include folk forms as well as the song-and-dance form called Mando.
source_name: Directorate of Art and Culture — Folk Tradition

title: Goan architecture
text: Goan architecture shows Indian and Portuguese influences in religious buildings and domestic houses.
source_name: Goa Department of Information — Art and Handicrafts

title: Goa's temples
text: Goa has important temple traditions, with well-known temples concentrated around Ponda and elsewhere in the state.

title: Shantadurga Temple
text: The Shantadurga Temple at Kavlem in Ponda taluka is an important Goan temple complex.
source_name: Government of Goa — Shanta Durga Temple

title: Goa's churches
text: Goa's church heritage includes the monumental churches and convents of Old Goa and active parish traditions across the state.
source_name: UNESCO — Churches and Convents of Goa

title: Forests and wildlife
text: Almost one-third of Goa is described as forested, supporting wildlife sanctuaries and varied Western Ghats habitats.
